title: Dance halls, picnics and West End
summary: He lists halls and picnic grounds, Spanish Fort, and long work at West End with Munson Hickman.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Where were some of the places you played when you started out? What kind of halls? Were they parties or picnics?

Well, I'll tell you, we played at the new hall. The Jean-Germy. The Artesian Hall. The Perseverance. The Economy Hall. The Corporate Hall. St. Catherine Hall. Oh, there's many others that I, you know, just slipped my memory.
Did you ever play many picnics like at Millenburg or anything out there?
Yeah, we used to play picnics at Millenburg, at the Little Evil Camp, the Bombay Lock. There's a lot of others that I, you know what I mean, the members, the names and God of Westman.
More roles. We used to play before the police, and the New Orleans had the police band. We used to play the eight day picnic every year. That was from Sunday to Sunday.
In your days when you started, was there anything going on in the Spanish Fort anymore? Was that touring?
Yeah. There was plenty of activities going around there, the Spanish Fort, but I mean, most of the white musicians had, colored musicians, didn't have nothing.

Well, West End, I worked at West End a good while. I worked at the Balloon with a fellow by the name of Munson Hickman, a saxophone player. And we worked at the Bungalow for a while. We left there and went to the C-Plan, and from the C-Plan we went to, well, another fellow used to be a racer around the island, called him Bill Wade. He had a nightclub out there. Well, I worked out there until they completely demolished all the camps. We were one of the last bands out there.
And who were you with out there?
Munson Hickman. Still with him? Uh-huh.
